text.p: President Clinton Sunday announced three federal programmes to fight breast cancer and other forms of the disease.

The initiatives call for a $30 million increase in funding for research into the genetics of breast cancer, creation of an Internet web site on the disease and establishment of a federal "Office of Cancer Survivorship" to study issues of concern to survivors of all cancers.
"These steps help us to put science at the service of our families and say we will do whatever it takes to continue the fight until there is a cure for cancer," Clinton said.
"I know about this from my own family's experience," Clinton said. His mother, Virginia Kelley, died of breast cancer in 1995.
Clinton announced the initiatives at a White House ceremony before leaving on a re-election campaign trip to Virginia and Tennessee.

The White House said that the $30 million was being shifted from other parts of the budget -- $20 million from an existing Defence Department breast cancer reseach fund and $10 million from a National Institutes of Health medical research fund.
"We are making progress," Clinton said, noting that the death rate from breast cancer had fallen for seven years in a row. But he added, "As far as we have come, we still have far to go."
Clinton also cited his efforts to curtail smoking by teenagers, saying, "We are working to get tobacco out of our children's lives forever."
